ESV.1: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the people of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house of the LORD.
ESV.2: The house that King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits  long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.
ESV.3: The vestibule in front of the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, equal to the width of the house, and ten cubits deep in front of the house.
ESV.4: And he made for the house windows with recessed frames.
ESV.5: He also built a structure  against the wall of the house, running around the walls of the house, both the nave and the inner sanctuary. And he made side chambers all around.
ESV.6: The lowest story  was five cubits broad, the middle one was six cubits broad, and the third was seven cubits broad. For around the outside of the house he made offsets on the wall in order that the supporting beams should not be inserted into the walls of the house.
ESV.7: When the house was built, it was with stone prepared at the quarry, so that neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard in the house while it was being built.
ESV.8: The entrance for the lowest  story was on the south side of the house, and one went up by stairs to the middle story, and from the middle story to the third.
ESV.9: So he built the house and finished it, and he made the ceiling of the house of beams and planks of cedar.
ESV.10: He built the structure against the whole house, five cubits high, and it was joined to the house with timbers of cedar.
ESV.11: Now the word of the LORD came to Solomon,
ESV.12: “Concerning this house that you are building, if you will walk in my statutes and obey my rules and keep all my commandments and walk in them, then I will establish my word with you, which I spoke to David your father.
ESV.13: And I will dwell among the children of Israel and will not forsake my people Israel.”
ESV.14: So Solomon built the house and finished it.
ESV.15: He lined the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar. From the floor of the house to the walls of the ceiling, he covered them on the inside with wood, and he covered the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
ESV.16: He built twenty cubits of the rear of the house with boards of cedar from the floor to the walls, and he built this within as an inner sanctuary, as the Most Holy Place.
ESV.17: The house, that is, the nave in front of the inner sanctuary, was forty cubits long.
ESV.18: The cedar within the house was carved in the form of gourds and open flowers. All was cedar; no stone was seen.
ESV.19: The inner sanctuary he prepared in the innermost part of the house, to set there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.
ESV.20: The inner sanctuary  was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high, and he overlaid it with pure gold. He also overlaid  an altar of cedar.
ESV.21: And Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with pure gold, and he drew chains of gold across, in front of the inner sanctuary, and overlaid it with gold.
ESV.22: And he overlaid the whole house with gold, until all the house was finished. Also the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.
ESV.23: In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olivewood, each ten cubits high.
ESV.24: Five cubits was the length of one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the length of the other wing of the cherub; it was ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
ESV.25: The other cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same measure and the same form.
ESV.26: The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was that of the other cherub.
ESV.27: He put the cherubim in the innermost part of the house. And the wings of the cherubim were spread out so that a wing of one touched the one wall, and a wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; their other wings touched each other in the middle of the house.
ESV.28: And he overlaid the cherubim with gold.
ESV.29: Around all the walls of the house he carved engraved figures of cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, in the inner and outer rooms.
ESV.30: The floor of the house he overlaid with gold in the inner and outer rooms.
ESV.31: For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of olivewood; the lintel and the doorposts were five-sided.
ESV.32: He covered the two doors of olivewood with carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers. He overlaid them with gold and spread gold on the cherubim and on the palm trees.
ESV.33: So also he made for the entrance to the nave doorposts of olivewood, in the form of a square,
ESV.34: and two doors of cypress wood. The two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the other door were folding.
ESV.35: On them he carved cherubim and palm trees and open flowers, and he overlaid them with gold evenly applied on the carved work.
ESV.36: He built the inner court with three courses of cut stone and one course of cedar beams.
ESV.37: In the fourth year the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid, in the month of Ziv.
ESV.38: And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was finished in all its parts, and according to all its specifications. He was seven years in building it.

NLT.1: It was in midspring, in the month of Ziv, during the fourth year of Solomon’s reign, that he began to construct the Temple of the LORD. This was 480 years after the people of Israel were rescued from their slavery in the land of Egypt.
NLT.2: The Temple that King Solomon built for the LORD was 90 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 45 feet high.
NLT.3: The entry room at the front of the Temple was 30 feet wide, running across the entire width of the Temple. It projected outward 15 feet from the front of the Temple.
NLT.4: Solomon also made narrow recessed windows throughout the Temple.
NLT.5: He built a complex of rooms against the outer walls of the Temple, all the way around the sides and rear of the building.
NLT.6: The complex was three stories high, the bottom floor being 7 1⁄2 feet wide, the second floor 9 feet wide, and the top floor 10 1⁄2 feet wide. The rooms were connected to the walls of the Temple by beams resting on ledges built out from the wall. So the beams were not inserted into the walls themselves.
NLT.7: The stones used in the construction of the Temple were finished at the quarry, so there was no sound of hammer, ax, or any other iron tool at the building site.
NLT.8: The entrance to the bottom floor was on the south side of the Temple. There were winding stairs going up to the second floor, and another flight of stairs between the second and third floors.
NLT.9: After completing the Temple structure, Solomon put in a ceiling made of cedar beams and planks.
NLT.10: As already stated, he built a complex of rooms along the sides of the building, attached to the Temple walls by cedar timbers. Each story of the complex was 7 1⁄2 feet high.
NLT.11: Then the LORD gave this message to Solomon:
NLT.12: “Concerning this Temple you are building, if you keep all my decrees and regulations and obey all my commands, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father, David.
NLT.13: I will live among the Israelites and will never abandon my people Israel.”
NLT.14: So Solomon finished building the Temple.
NLT.15: The entire inside, from floor to ceiling, was paneled with wood. He paneled the walls and ceilings with cedar, and he used planks of cypress for the floors.
NLT.16: He partitioned off an inner sanctuary — the Most Holy Place — at the far end of the Temple. It was 30 feet deep and was paneled with cedar from floor to ceiling.
NLT.17: The main room of the Temple, outside the Most Holy Place, was 60 feet long.
NLT.18: Cedar paneling completely covered the stone walls throughout the Temple, and the paneling was decorated with carvings of gourds and open flowers.
NLT.19: He prepared the inner sanctuary at the far end of the Temple, where the Ark of the LORD’s Covenant would be placed.
NLT.20: This inner sanctuary was 30 feet long, 30 feet wide, and 30 feet high. He overlaid the inside with solid gold. He also overlaid the altar made of cedar.
NLT.21: Then Solomon overlaid the rest of the Temple’s interior with solid gold, and he made gold chains to protect the entrance to the Most Holy Place.
NLT.22: So he finished overlaying the entire Temple with gold, including the altar that belonged to the Most Holy Place.
NLT.23: He made two cherubim of wild olive wood, each 15 feet tall, and placed them in the inner sanctuary.
NLT.24: The wingspan of each of the cherubim was 15 feet, each wing being 7 1⁄2 feet long.
NLT.25: The two cherubim were identical in shape and size;
NLT.27: He placed them side by side in the inner sanctuary of the Temple. Their outspread wings reached from wall to wall, while their inner wings touched at the center of the room.
NLT.28: He overlaid the two cherubim with gold.
NLT.29: He decorated all the walls of the inner sanctuary and the main room with carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.
NLT.30: He overlaid the floor in both rooms with gold.
NLT.31: For the entrance to the inner sanctuary, he made double doors of wild olive wood with five-sided doorposts.
NLT.32: These double doors were decorated with carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers. The doors, including the decorations of cherubim and palm trees, were overlaid with gold.
NLT.33: Then he made four-sided doorposts of wild olive wood for the entrance to the Temple.
NLT.34: There were two folding doors of cypress wood, and each door was hinged to fold back upon itself.
NLT.35: These doors were decorated with carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers — all overlaid evenly with gold.
NLT.36: The walls of the inner courtyard were built so that there was one layer of cedar beams between every three layers of finished stone.
NLT.37: The foundation of the LORD’s Temple was laid in midspring, in the month of Ziv, during the fourth year of Solomon’s reign.
NLT.38: The entire building was completed in every detail by midautumn, in the month of Bul, during the eleventh year of his reign. So it took seven years to build the Temple.

AMP.1: Now it came about in the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv (April-May) which is the second month, that he began to build the Lord's house (temple).
AMP.2: The length of the house which King Solomon built for the LORD was sixty cubits (90 ft.), its width twenty (30 ft.), and its height thirty cubits (45 ft.).
AMP.3: The porch in front of the main room of the house (temple) was twenty cubits long, corresponding to the width of the house, and its depth in front of the house was ten cubits.
AMP.4: He also made framed (artistic) window openings for the house.
AMP.5: Against the wall of the house he built extensions around the walls of the house, around both the main room (Holy Place) and the Holy of Holies; and he made side chambers all around.
AMP.6: The lowest story was five cubits wide, the middle was six cubits wide, and the third was seven cubits wide; for he made offsets (niches) in the walls all around on the outside of the house so that the supporting beams would not be inserted into the walls of the house.
AMP.7: While it was being built, the house was built of stone prepared and finished (precut) at the quarry, and no hammer, axe, or iron tool of any kind was heard in the house while it was under construction.
AMP.8: The entrance to the lowest side chamber was on the right [or south] side of the house; and they would go up winding stairs to the middle [level], and from the middle to the third.
AMP.9: So Solomon built the house (temple) and finished it, and roofed the house with beams and boards of cedar.
AMP.10: Then he built the extensions [of rooms] against the entire house, each [story] five cubits high; and they were attached to the house with timbers of cedar.
AMP.11: Now the word of the LORD came to Solomon, saying,
AMP.12: "Concerning this house which you are building, if you will walk in My statutes and execute My precepts and keep all My commandments by walking in them, then I will carry out My word (promises) with you which I made to David your father.
AMP.13: I will dwell among the sons (descendants) of Israel, and will not abandon My people Israel."
AMP.14: So Solomon built the house (temple) and finished it.
AMP.15: He built the walls of the interior of the house [that is, the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies] with boards of cedar, from the floor of the house to the rafters of the ceiling. He overlaid the interior with wood, and he overlaid the floor of the house with boards of cypress.
AMP.16: He built twenty cubits on the rear of the house with boards of cedar from the floor to the ceiling; he built its interior as the [inner] sanctuary, the Holy of Holies.
AMP.17: The [rest of the] house, that is, the temple in front of the Holy of Holies, was forty cubits long.
AMP.18: The cedar on the house within had wood carvings in the shape of gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar; no stone was visible.
AMP.19: Then he prepared the Holy of Holies within the house in order to put the ark of the covenant of the LORD there.
AMP.20: The Holy of Holies was twenty cubits in length, twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in height (a cube), and he overlaid it with pure gold. He also overlaid the cedar altar [with gold].
AMP.21: Solomon overlaid the interior of the house with pure gold, and he drew chains of gold across the front of the Holy of Holies (inner sanctuary), and he overlaid it with gold.
AMP.22: Then he overlaid the entire house with gold, until the whole house was finished. He also overlaid the entire [incense] altar which was by the Holy of Holies with gold.
AMP.23: Within the Holy of Holies he made two cherubim (sculptured figures) of olive wood, each ten cubits high.
AMP.24: One wing of the cherub was five cubits long, and the other wing was also five cubits long; it was ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.
AMP.25: The [wingspan of the] other cherub was also ten cubits. The measurements and cut (shape) of the two cherubim were the same;
AMP.26: the height of the one cherub was ten cubits, as was the other.
AMP.27: He put the cherubim [above the ark] inside the innermost room of the house, and their wings were spread out so that the wing of the one touched one wall, and the wing of the other cherub was touching the other wall; and their inner wings were touching each other in the middle of the house.
AMP.28: Solomon also overlaid the cherubim with gold.
AMP.29: He carved all the walls of the house all around with carved engravings of cherubim, palm-shaped decorations, and open flowers, [both] the inner and the outer sanctuaries.
AMP.30: He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, [both] the inner and outer sanctuaries.
AMP.31: For the entrance of the Holy of Holies he made two [folding] doors of olive wood, the lintel (header above the door) and five-sided doorposts (frames).
AMP.32: So he made two doors of olive wood, and he carved on them carvings of cherubim, palm-shaped decorations, and open flowers; and overlaid them with gold; and he hammered out overlays of gold on the cherubim and palm decorations.
AMP.33: Also he made for the entrance of the [outer] sanctuary (the Holy Place) four-sided doorposts (frames) of olive wood
AMP.34: and two doors of cypress wood; the two leaves of the one door turned on pivots and were folding, and the two leaves of the other door also turned on pivots.
AMP.35: He carved cherubim, palm-shaped decorations, and open flowers on the doors, and overlaid them with gold evenly applied on the carved work.
AMP.36: He built the inner courtyard with three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams.
AMP.37: In the fourth year [of King Solomon's reign] the foundation of the Lord's house was laid, in the [second] month, Ziv (April-May).
AMP.38: In the eleventh year [of King Solomon's reign] in the month of Bul (October-November), that is, the eighth month, the house was finished throughout all its parts and in accordance with all its specifications. So he built it in seven years.

NIV.25: The second cherub also measured ten cubits, for the two cherubim were identical in size and shape.
NIV.26: The height of each cherub was ten cubits.

NIV.28: He overlaid the cherubim with gold.
NIV.29: On the walls all around the temple, in both the inner and outer rooms, he carved cherubim, palm trees and open flowers.
NIV.30: He also covered the floors of both the inner and outer rooms of the temple with gold.
NIV.31: For the entrance of the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood with five-sided jambs.

NIV.37: The foundation of the temple of the Lord was laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.
